examples.description: A user connects to an unsecured Wi-Fi network at a busy cafe to check their email and browse social media. An attacker, connected to the same network, uses a packet sniffer to capture unencrypted HTTP traffic, including login credentials and session cookies. The attacker then uses this data to hijack the user's online accounts.
indicators: Connection to an open, unsecured Wi-Fi network with no password
Presence of unencrypted HTTP traffic in captured packets
Multiple login credentials and session tokens intercepted
Same network subnet for attacker and victim
Sudden unauthorized access to user accounts after public Wi-Fi use

examples.description: An attacker sets up a rogue Wi-Fi hotspot named similarly to a popular airport’s official network. Unsuspecting travelers connect to this fake access point. The attacker intercepts all transmitted data, including sensitive information like credit card numbers and personal identification details, then manipulates traffic to redirect users to phishing sites.
indicators: Wi-Fi network SSID closely mimics a legitimate public hotspot
High volume of intercepted HTTPS traffic downgraded to HTTP
Unusual DNS responses or redirects to suspicious websites
User complaints about unexpected login prompts or warnings
Network traffic shows man-in-the-middle proxy behavior

examples.description: An employee connects their laptop to an unsecured public Wi-Fi network at an airport without a VPN. An attacker on the same network uses ARP spoofing to position themselves between the employee’s device and the network gateway. The attacker captures sensitive corporate emails and internal documents transmitted over the network.
indicators: Use of ARP spoofing or poisoning to intercept traffic
Sensitive corporate data transmitted without encryption
Employee connected to unsecured public Wi-Fi without VPN
Network logs show unusual routing or duplicate MAC addresses
Exfiltrated data includes confidential company information
